'''Hans J. van Ommeren Dekker''' (born 18 January 1947 in [[Amsterdam]], Netherlands) is a Dutch [[theoretical physicist]] in the line of [[Dirk Polder]], [[Ralph Kronig]], and [[Nico van Kampen]]. His scientific work inter alia involves [[laser]] theory, [[Path integral formulation|path integrals]] in [[curved space]]s, [[nonequilibrium statistical mechanics]], [[dissipation]] in [[quantum mechanics]], and [[hydrodynamic]] [[turbulence]]. He was director of the Private [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Amsterdam and is professor emeritus at the Institute for Theoretical Physics of the [[University of Amsterdam]].

== Biography ==

Dekker studied physics at [[Delft University of Technology]], in [[Delft]], Netherlands, where he did research in [[acoustics]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Dekker | first1=H. | title=EDGE effect measurements in a reverberation room | journal=Journal of Sound and Vibration | date=1974 | volume=32 | issue=2 | pages=199–202 | doi=10.1016/S0022-460X(74)80164-1 | bibcode=1974JSV....32..199D }}</ref> in the group of Cornelis W. Kosten, and in [[electron optics]]<ref>{{cite book | last1=Glaser | first1=Walter | title=Grundlagen der Elektronenoptik | date=January 1952 | publisher=Springer | isbn=978-3-662-23620-8 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Dekker | first1=H. | title=A new method of measuring the axial field distribution in a superconducting electron lens by means of the Faraday effect | journal=Journal of Physics E: Scientific Instruments | date=1972 | volume=5 | issue=4 | pages=368–372 | doi=10.1088/0022-3735/5/4/021 | bibcode=1972JPhE....5..368D }}</ref> with [[:nl:Jan Bart Le Poole]].

In 1968 he was also chief editor of the Delft student periodical Het Orakel (for which he inter alia wrote a story <ref>H. Dekker, Hartstocht [Heart passage/passion], Orakel (Delftse Uitgeversmaatschappij, 1960) May 28, p. 8. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333448952</ref> about the first successful heart transplant by [[Christiaan Barnard]], [[Kaapstad]], South Africa) while he spent the summer of 1970 with an [[IAESTE]]/[[Nuffic]] grant working on [[thermoluminescent dosimeter]]s <ref>J. R. Cameron, N. Suntharalingam and G. N. Kennedy, Thermoluminescent Dosimetry (Univ. of Wisconsin Press, 1968).</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Some aspects of a CaF2:Mn thermoluminescent dosimeter |journal=Health Physics |date=1976 |volume=30 |issue=5 |pages=399–401 |pmid= 1270268 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/21885971}}</ref> at [[Tennessee Valley Authority]] (TVA), [[Muscle Shoals, Alabama]], United States.<ref>H. Klebanoff, Americans Search for Reasons to be Proud [Says Holland Student], ''The Florence Times'' (Florence/Muscle Shoals, Alabama, USA) August 5, 1970, p. 4. [https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dekker1970.pdf]</ref>

He completed his studies in [[theoretical physics]] under the supervision of [[Dirk Polder]] ([[solid-state physics]]<ref>H. Dekker, Enkele aspekten van helikongolven (Some aspects of helicon waves), Delft University of Technology, Faculty of Science Report, 43 pages (1969) [https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dekker1969.pdf]</ref>), [[Ralph Kronig]] ([[quantum electrodynamics]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=A theory of cooperative effects in stimulated Cerenkov radiation |journal=Physica B+C |date=1977 |volume=90 |issue=2 |pages=283–291 |doi=10.1016/0378-4363(77)90121-8 |bibcode=1977PhyBC..90..283D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240908572}}</ref>), and Jaap Kokkedee <ref>J.J.J. Kokkedee, Academic Tree [https://academictree.org/physics/tree.php?pid=62893] [https://www.vvtp.tudelft.nl/en/news/death-of-prof-dr-ir-jjj-kokkedee]</ref> ([[quantum field theory]]<ref>https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/301480588</ref> and [[general relativity]]<ref>H. Dekker, Algemene Relativiteits Theorie (General Theory of Relativity), Lecture notes, Delft University of Technology (Faculty of Science, J.J.J. Kokkedee, 1974) [https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dekker1974.pdf]</ref>).

Dekker then joined the staff of the Netherlands Physics Laboratory [[Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research|TNO]],<ref>[[Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research|TNO]] [https://www.tno.nl/en/about-tno/locations/]</ref> in [[The Hague]], where he became head of the Theoretical Physics Group in 1971. Of prime interest at that time was the quantum theory of the [[laser]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Stationary momentum space solution of the Fokker-Planck equation for a simple model of a laser oscillator exhibiting spatial dispersion |journal=Optics Communications |date=1974 |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=114–119 |doi=10.1016/0030-4018(74)90034-0 |bibcode=1974OptCo..10..114D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/243211788}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=The Fokker-Planck equations for the continuum mode laser with spatially inhomogenous dissipation and excitation |journal=Physica B+C |date=1976 |volume=83 |issue=2 |pages=183–192 |doi=10.1016/0378-4363(76)90220-5 |bibcode=1976PhyBC..83..183D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240908429}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Stationary solution of the Fokker-Planck equation for the continuum mode laser with spatially inhomogeneous dissipation and excitation |journal=Physica B+C |date=1976 |volume=83 |issue=2 |pages=193–199 |doi=10.1016/0378-4363(76)90221-7 |bibcode=1976PhyBC..83..193D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240908430}}</ref> and in the early seventies he thus got involved in the [[Synergetics (Haken)|Synergetics]]<ref>H. Dekker, Synergetica: Coöperatieve verschijnselen in complexe systemen, Intermediair, 31 (1975) 11, 32 (1975) 31. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274371628]</ref> summerschools in [[Erice]], [[Sicily]], Italy, on co-operative phenomena in [[complex system]]s,<ref>H. Dekker, Coöperatieve Verschijnselen in Complexe Systemen, TNO Project 4, 6 (1976) 239-243. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275639637]</ref> and in 1976 he was visiting scientist at the [[University of Stuttgart]], Germany, in the group of [[Hermann Haken]]. In the later seventies his interest in stochastic laser theory lead to several papers on path integrals for nonlinear processes,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Time-local gaussian processes, path integrals and nonequilibrium nonlinear diffusion |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |date=1976 |volume=85 |issue=2 |pages=363–373 |doi=10.1016/0378-4371(76)90055-8 |bibcode=1976PhyA...85..363D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/222356887}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Wiegel | first1=Frederik W. | title=Introduction to Path-integral Methods in Physics and Polymer Science | date=1986 | publisher=World Scientific | isbn=9971-978-70-9 }}</ref> also in curved Riemannian spaces.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Functional integration in Riemannian geometries revisited |journal=Physical Review A |date=1980 |volume=22 |issue=3 |pages=1315–1316 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.22.1315 |bibcode=1980PhRvA..22.1315D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/238974128}}</ref><ref>H. Dekker, Quantization in Curved Spaces: Functional Integration and the Quantum Action Principle in Riemannian Geometries, in "Functional Integration: Theory and Applications", Edited by JP. Antoine & E. Tirapegui (Plenum, New York, 1980) 207-224. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274371349]</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Proof of identity of Graham and Dekker covariant lattice propagators |journal=Physical Review A |date=1981 |volume=24 |issue=6 |pages=3182–3187 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.24.3182 |bibcode=1981PhRvA..24.3182D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/238300726}}</ref> Meanwhile he also proposed a mathematical model in theoretical biology on rodent [[population dynamics]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Myers | first1=Judith H. | last2=Krebs | first2=Charles J. | title=Population Cycles in Rodents | journal=Scientific American | date=1974 | volume=230 | issue=6 | pages=38–47 | doi=10.1038/scientificamerican0674-38 | jstor=24950096 | pmid=4833320 | bibcode=1974SciAm.230f..38M }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=A simple mathematical model of rodent population cycles |journal=Journal of Mathematical Biology |date=1975 |volume=2 |pages=57–67 |doi=10.1007/BF00276016 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/226829305}}</ref><ref>H. Dekker, On the Master Equation Approach to Rodent Population Cycles, General Systems, Vol. XXII (1977) 113-118 [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276957492]</ref>

In 1980 he received a Ph.D. in theoretical physics from [[Nico van Kampen]]<ref>[https://academictree.org/physics/tree.php?pid=4062 N.G. van Kampen, Academic Tree]</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |last2=Van Kampen |first2=N.G |title=Eigenvalues of a diffusion process with a critical point |journal=Physics Letters A |date=1979 |volume=73 |issue=5–6 |pages=374–376 |doi=10.1016/0375-9601(79)90088-4 |bibcode=1979PhLA...73..374D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/222450745}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |last2=Van Kampen |first2=N.G. |title=The expansion of the Fokker-Planck equation including a critical point |journal=Physics Letters A |date=1980 |volume=76 |issue=2 |pages=101–103 |doi=10.1016/0375-9601(80)90580-0 |bibcode=1980PhLA...76..101D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/27707210}}</ref>  at [[Utrecht University]], Netherlands, concerning the systematic expansion of the master equation for [[Markov process|Markov]] [[stochastic processes]] including a [[Critical point (mathematics)|critical point]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Critical dynamics the expansion of the master equation including a critical point |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |date=1980 |volume=103 |issue=1–2 |pages=55–79 |doi=10.1016/0378-4371(80)90207-1 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/238948067}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Critical dynamics the expansion of the master equation including a critical point |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |date=1980 |volume=103 |issue=1–2 |pages=80–98 |doi=10.1016/0378-4371(80)90208-3 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/243355515}}</ref> (see also <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=On the critical point of a Malthus–Verhulst process |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=1980 |volume=72 |issue=1 |pages=189–191 |doi=10.1063/1.438901 |bibcode=1980JChPh..72..189D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/234847231}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Unstable state dynamics: A systematic evaluation of the master equation |journal=Physics Letters A |date=1982 |volume=88 |issue=6 |pages=279–281 |doi=10.1016/0375-9601(82)90068-8 |bibcode=1982PhLA...88..279D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/232354251}}</ref>). At about the same time Dekker wrote his monograph 'Classical and quantum mechanics of the damped harmonic oscillator', published in 1981 as a [[Physics Reports]] volume,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Classical and quantum mechanics of the damped harmonic oscillator |journal=Physics Reports |date=1981 |volume=80 |issue=1 |pages=1–110 |doi=10.1016/0370-1573(81)90033-8 |bibcode=1981PhR....80....1D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/222990789}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Index |journal=Physics Reports |date=1981 |volume=80 |issue=1 |pages=110–112 |doi=10.1016/0370-1573(81)90034-X |bibcode=1981PhR....80..110. |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280075501}}</ref> which has become a standard reference for [[dissipation]] in [[quantum mechanics]].

During 1981–1982 Dekker was [[NATO]]/[[Fulbright]] visiting professor at the Department of Chemistry, at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in [[Boston]], United States, with [[:de:Irwin Oppenheim]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |last2=Oppenheim |first2=I. |title=Two-dimensional random walk description of fluid flow in the presence of a wall: The origin of stick versus slip boundary conditions in the continuum limit |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |date=1983 |volume=117 |issue=1 |pages=1–16 |doi=10.1016/0378-4371(83)90018-3 |bibcode=1983PhyA..117....1D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/222066069}}</ref> and at the [[University of California, San Diego]] (UCSD), in [[La Jolla]], United States, with Kurt E. Shuler.<ref>[https://www.geni.com/people/Prof-Kurt-Shuler-Schulherr/6000000056703197825 K.E. Shuler, Biography]</ref> He further was guest scientist at [[IBM]] [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center]], [[Yorktown Heights]] United States, in 1988, with [[Rolf Landauer]] (on [[nonequilibrium statistical mechanics|nonequilibrium]] [[stochastic process]]es<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |last2=Maassen Van Den Brink |first2=A. |title=Nonisothermal activation: Nonlinear transport theory |journal=Superlattices and Microstructures |date=1998 |volume=23 |issue=3–4 |pages=479–494 |doi=10.1006/spmi.1997.0510 |bibcode=1998SuMi...23..479D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2355651}}</ref>) and [[Martin Gutzwiller]] (on [[functional integration]]<ref>{{cite book | last1=Gutzwiller | first1=Martin C. | title=Chaos in Classical and Quantum Mechanics | date=August 1991 | publisher=Springer | isbn=978-0-387-97173-5 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Lundqvist | first1=Stig | title=Path Summation: Achievements and Goals : Proceedings of the Adriatico Research Conference on "Path Integral Method with Applications", Trieste, 1-4 September, 1987 | date=1988 | publisher=World Scientific | isbn=9971-50-597-5 }}</ref>). From 1985 through 1991 he also was external reviewer in the group of Rudolf de Bruyn Ouboter at the [[:nl:Kamerlingh Onnes Laboratorium]] ([[Leiden University]]) concerning research on macroscopic [[quantum interference]] phenomena in [[Josephson junction]] devices.

In 1989 he became [[Lorentz]]-[[:nl:van Iterson]] Professor at the Institute for Theoretical Physics (at the time headed by [[Hans Capel]]) of the [[University of Amsterdam]]. His inaugural lecture <ref>H. Dekker, Zekere Beperkingen, Oratie Universiteit van Amsterdam 1992 (Printed Edition: FEL-TNO, Den Haag) p. 1-23. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286937869]</ref> (English title: ‘Certain limitations’) is a plea for the concept of stochastic processes, both classical and quantum mechanical (see, e.g., the Capita selecta on 'Dissipative quantum processes' <ref>H. Dekker, Poster/synopsis of Lectures on 'Dissipatieve quantum processen', University of Amsterdam, 1990/1994 [https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dekker1990.pdf]</ref>  and also the book chapter ‘An educated game of chance in physics’ <ref>H. Dekker, From Microscopia to Macroscopia: An Educated “Game of Chance” in Physics, in: “Chance and Uncertainty”, Edited by [[Hans Capel|H.W. Capel]] et al. (Vossiuspers/[[Amsterdam University Press]] AUP, Amsterdam, 1995) p. 87-105. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/241858507]</ref>).

Dekker inter alia was visiting professor at the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) in [[Trieste]], Italy, in 1987 and 1996 (with [[Lawrence Schulman]],<ref>{{cite book | last1=Schulman | first1=L. S. | title=Techniques and Applications of Path Integration | date=17 February 1981 | publisher=Wiley | isbn=0-471-76450-7 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Lundqvist | first1=Stig | title=Path Summation: Achievements and Goals : Proceedings of the Adriatico Research Conference on "Path Integral Method with Applications", Trieste, 1-4 September, 1987 | date=1988 | publisher=World Scientific | isbn=9971-50-597-5 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Mugnai | first1=D. | last2=Ranfagni | first2=A. | last3=Schulman | first3=Lawrence S. | title=Tunneling and Its Implications | date=1997 | publisher=World Scientific | isbn=981-02-2905-4 }}</ref> on dissipative [[quantum tunneling]];<ref>H. Dekker, The Frozen False Vacuum, in: Path Summation - Achievements and Goals, Edited by S. Lundqvist, A. Ranfagni, V. Sa-yakanit, and L.S. Schulman (World Scientific, Singapore, 1988) p. 147-167. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/293803720] {{ISBN|9971-50-597-5}}</ref><ref>H. Dekker, Multilevel Mesoscopic Tunneling, in: Tunneling and its Implications, Edited by D. Mugnai, A. Ranfagni, and L.S. Schulman (World Scientific, Singapore, 1997) p. 66-79. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/241857239] {{ISBN|981-0229054}}</ref> see also <ref>H. Dekker, Dissipative Quantum Decay at Weak Bias: Finite Temperature Tunneling through Almost Degenerate Barriers, in: Path Integrals from meV to MeV, Edited by V. Sa-yakanit, W. Sritrakool, J.O. Berananda, M.C. Gutzwiller, A. Inomata, S. Lundqvist, J.R. Klauder, and L.S. Schulman (World Scientific, Singapore, 1990) p. 329-354. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286935396] {{ISBN|9971-50-935-0}}</ref><ref>H. Dekker, Dissipative Quantum Processes, in: Path Integrals in Physics, Edited by V. Sa-yakanit, J.O. Berananda, and W. Sritrakool (World Scientific, Singapore, 1994) p. 137-153. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301232236] {{ISBN|981-0220707}}</ref>) and invited lecturer at the Centennial Meeting of the Fondation [[Schlumberger]]/[[Louis de Broglie]] in [[:fr:Les Treilles]], France, in 1992 <ref>[https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dekker1992.pdf Poster of the Louis de Broglie Centennial Meeting, France, 1992]</ref> (with [[Tony Leggett]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Leggett | first1=A. J. | last2=Garg | first2=Anupam | title=Quantum mechanics versus macroscopic realism: Is the flux there when nobody looks? | journal=Physical Review Letters | date=1985 | volume=54 | issue=9 | pages=857–860 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.857 | pmid=10031639 | bibcode=1985PhRvL..54..857L }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Leggett | first1=A. J. | last2=Chakravarty | first2=S. | last3=Dorsey | first3=A. T. | last4=Fisher | first4=Matthew P. A. | last5=Garg | first5=Anupam | last6=Zwerger | first6=W. | title=Dynamics of the dissipative two-state system | journal=Reviews of Modern Physics | date=1987 | volume=59 | pages=1–85 | doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.59.1 | hdl=2142/94708 | hdl-access=free }}</ref> on '[[Mesoscopic physics]]: from dissipative [[quantum mechanics]] to [[non-equilibrium thermodynamics]]' <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Noninteracting-blip approximation for a two-level system coupled to a heat bath |journal=Physical Review A |date=1987 |volume=35 |issue=3 |pages=1436–1437 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.35.1436 |pmid=9898290 |bibcode=1987PhRvA..35.1436D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/13391422}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Exactly solvable model for thermal activation and quantum tunneling in Ohmic systems |journal=Physical Review A |date=1988 |volume=38 |issue=12 |pages=6351–6361 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.38.6351 |pmid=9900393 |bibcode=1988PhRvA..38.6351D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/13389525}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Multilevel tunneling and coherence: Dissipative spin-hopping dynamics at finite temperatures |journal=Physical Review A |date=1991 |volume=44 |issue=4 |pages=2314–2323 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.44.2314 |pmid=9906212 |bibcode=1991PhRvA..44.2314D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/13383344}} {{erratum|doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.50.4265|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/13317301|checked=yes}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |last2=Maassen Van Den Brink |first2=Alec |title=Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Mesoscopic Systems |journal=Journal of Superconductivity |date=1999 |volume=12 |issue=6 |pages=719–725 |doi=10.1023/A:1007772623750 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/226442452}}</ref><ref>H. Dekker, Multilevel macroscopic quantum tunneling: coherence and dissipation, in: Controllable dissipative tunneling - Tunnel transport in low-dimensional systems, Edited by A.J. Leggett (Fizmatlit, Moscow, 2012) p. 327-341 [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301540854] [https://www.rfbr.ru/rffi/ru/books/o_1780081#307] [http://artlib.osu.ru/web/books/content_all/362.pdf] {{ISBN|978-5922113625}}</ref>).

From 1998-2018 Dekker also was director of the Private [[Institute for Advanced Study]], in [[Amsterdam]], where he inter alia worked on the stochastic theory of [[hydrodynamic]] [[turbulence]]<ref>{{cite book |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Turbulence Modeling and Vortex Dynamics |chapter=Boundary-layer turbulence modeling and vorticity dynamics: II. Towards a theory of turbulent shear flow? |series=Lecture Notes in Physics |date=1997 |volume=491 |pages=238–241 |doi=10.1007/BFb0105040 |isbn=978-3-540-63051-7 |chapter-url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/225589132}}</ref><ref>H. Dekker, Theory of hydrodynamic turbulence: External scales and irrotational fields, in: Progress in Statistical Mechanics Research, Edited by J.S. Moreno (Nova Science Publishers, New York, 2008) p. 349-372 [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/254917457]</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dekker |first1=H. |title=Turbulence: Large-scale sweeping and the emergence of small-scale Kolmogorov spectra |journal=Physical Review E |date=2011 |volume=84 |issue=2 |article-number=026302 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.84.026302 |pmid=21929085 |bibcode=2011PhRvE..84b6302D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/51653479}}</ref><ref>H. Dekker, Mathematical Modelling of Hydrodynamic Turbulence: Large Scale Sweeping and the Emergence of Small Scale Kolmogorov Spectra, in: Mathematical Modelling, Edited by C.R. Brennan (Nova Science Publishers, New York, 2012) p. 351-425. [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287264174]</ref>.

* [[Nuffic]] Physics Award and Grant (1970)
* J.B. Le Poole [[:nl:Jan Bart Le Poole]] Science Award (Delft, 1971)
* [[Royal Dutch Society of Science]] Award (1981)
* [[Fulbright Foundation]] Science Award (1981)
* [[NATO]] Fellowship Award (1981/1982)
* Van Schooneveld [[Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research|TNO]] [[Netherlands Organization for Applied Scientific Research]] Prize and Medal (The Hague, 1992)
* Panta Rhei Award (J.M. Burgers [[:nl:Jan Burgers (natuurkundige)]] Centre [https://jmburgerscentum.nl], 1994)
* [[Lawrence Schulman]] Award ([[ICTP]] [[Trieste]], 1996)
* [[AkzoNobel]] Science Prize Nomination (1999)
* J.E. Hamilton Foundation [https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-hamilton-of-silvertonhill] Physics Award (2009)
